entries.toelichting: Conjunctive waw prefix. Syntactic base-connector. 'And' covers the additive function; context may imply 'but' or 'then', but concordantly 'and' is held as the base rendering.
Definite article prefix. 'The' as the English definite article; English does not inflect for gender/number, so the rendering is uniform.
Proclitic preposition. Dative/direction: to, for, towards, unto. 'To' preserves the dative-directional core; 'for' or 'unto' are context-splinters of the same particle.
Proclitic preposition. Locative-instrumental: in, on, with, through. 'In' as core locative; extensions depend on context.
Shortened form of min (H4480a) as prefix. 'From' as the ablative core; 'out of' is an alternative for the full-form min. Concordantly 'from' for the prefix variant.
Proclitic preposition of comparison. 'As' covers the comparative core; 'like' (H3644, H834d) is an independent lexeme.
Interrogative prefix (homograph with the definite article Hd, but functionally distinct). Concordantly rendered as the question mark '?' in rendering; English has no prefixal interrogative form.
Proclitic relative (late-Hebrew form, related to asher H834a). Concordantly 'which' as primary form; 'that' or 'who' are grammatical context-variants.
Root 'b. Basic kinship term; parallel em (mother, H517).
Aramaic cognate of H1 av 'father' (Dan 2:23; 5:2,11,13,18; Ezra 4:15; 5:12). Concordantly linked via the '-aramaic' suffix.
The green young plant or shoot - Job 8:12 (he is still in his greenness, not cut off) and Song of Songs 6:11 (to see the young shoots); also the Aramaic 'fruit' in Daniel 4:11-12.

Dan-aramaic-fruit-tree-abundant and Dan-aramaic-fruit-of-it-eat and Dan-aramaic-growing-fruit (Dan 4:9,11,18,21). Hyphenated to distinguish the fruit-aramaic-aspect from H6529 peri-Hebrew 'fruit' (already assigned); aramaic-cognate-tree-fruits.
Proper noun, fourth eunuch attendant of Ahasuerus; Esth 1:10; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abagtha.

Qal: be lost, perish, vanish. Pi'el and Hiph'il: cause to perish, destroy. The common kernel is 'to no longer exist where one was'. Used both for lost objects (a sheep, Lev 5:23) and for perishing persons (Num 24:20). Hyphenated to preserve the dual-aspect; 'perish' alone leaves the lost-object sense underweight.
Aramaic cognate of H6 avad 'perish' (Dan 2:12,18,24; 4:33; 7:11,26; Ezra 6:12; 7:26; Jer 10:11). Concordantly linked via '-aramaic' suffix to mark the cognate.

Num-end-Amalek-is-unto-perishing and Num-unto-Asshur-shall-carry-captives-and-Eber-shall-see-perishing (Num 24:20,24). Hyphenated to distinguish the perishing-lost-going-down aspect from H9 oved-aramaic 'servant' (already assigned); family with H6 avad 'perish-be-lost' (already assigned) - Balaam-nations-oracles-going-down.

Mislaid object or loss-of-property (Ex 22:8; Lev 5:22,23; Deut 22:3; Isa 11:11). Hyphenated to distinguish the loss-mislaid aspect from H7665 shever 'breaking'; family with H6 avad 'perish-pass-away'.
Destructive ruin as abstract noun - Proverbs 27:20 (Sheol and destruction are never satisfied) and Numbers 24:20 (his end is unto destruction); extended nominal form of H6 avad (perish).

Place of perdition alongside Sheol and death (Job 26:6; 28:22; 31:12; Ps 88:12; Prov 15:11; 27:20). Hyphenated to distinguish the perdition-destruction-place-aspect from H7585 sheol 'sheol' (already assigned) and H4194 maweth 'death' (already assigned); family with H6 avad 'perish' (already assigned). External-reference NT: Rev 9:11 transliterates as Abaddon (Greek Apollyon).
Hapax: Jews-defeated-enemies unto destruction; Esth 9:5.
Esther: how-shall-I-look-on-the-perishing-of-my-people; Esth 8:6.
Qal: consent, be willing; mostly negated (be unwilling); root of evyon (needy); concordantly 'be-willing'. Distinguished from H7521 ratsah 'delight-in' and H2654 chafets 'desire'.
Hapax form; Job-transgression unto-full-ripening; Job 34:36.
Swift-reed-skiffs with which Job's-days fly away; Job 9:26.
Hapax Prov 23:29 who-has-woe outcry-lament; onomatopoeic.

The feeding-trough or manger of livestock - Proverbs 14:4 (where there are no oxen, the manger is empty), Isaiah 1:3 (the ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's manger) and Job 39:9 (will the wild ox lodge by your manger?).
Sword-flashing-stroke at city-gates; Eze 21:15.
Egyptian fruit-craving; Num 11:5.
Proper noun, mother of Hezekiah; 2Kgs 18:2; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abi.

1S-Kish-the-son-of-Abiel-the-son-of-Zeror and 1S-Kish-Saul's-father-and-Ner-Abner's-father-son-of-Abiel (1S 9:1; 14:51). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abiel-grandfather-Saul-Benjamin-aspect from other Abi-names; family with H1 av 'father' (already assigned) - 'my-father-is-God'-theophoric-grandfather-Saul-genealogy-Benjamin.
Proper noun, son of Korah; Ex 6:24; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abiasaph.
Fresh ear-stage of barley; also the name of the Passover-month (Ex 9:31; 13:4; 23:15; 34:18; Deut 16:1; Lev 2:14). Hyphenated to bind the agronomical reference (ear-on-stalk) to the month-meaning.
Proper noun ('my-father-is-joy'); wife of Nabal, later of David; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abigail.
Benjamite tribe-head at the Sinai-numbering (Num 1:11; 2:22; 7:60,65; 10:24). English convention: Abidan. 'My-father-judges'.

Gen-sons-Midian-Ephah-Epher-Henoch-Abida-Eldaah and 1Chr-sons-Midian-Abida (Gen 25:4; 1Chr 1:33). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abida-son-Midian-Abraham-grandson-aspect from other theophoric-names; Midianite-line-third-generation-Abraham.
Proper noun ('my-father-is-YHWH'); multiple persons; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abijah.

Second son of Aaron and Elisheba (Ex 6:23, 24:1,9, 28:1); offered strange fire with Nadab and was consumed together with him (Lev 10:1-2, Num 3:2,4, 26:60-61, 1Chr 6:3, 24:1-2); 'He-is-Father'; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abihu.
Proper noun, Benjamin tribe-head, son of Bela; 1Chr 8:3; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abihud.
Several persons in Levitical and royal genealogies (Num 3:35; 1Chr 2:29; 5:14; 2Chr 11:18; Esth 2:15; 9:29). 'My-father-is-strength'. English convention: Abihail.
Abiezrite-Gideon's-clan and Gideon-burial-place (Judg 6:11,24; 8:32). English convention: Abiezrite. Family with H44 Aviezer 'Abiezer' (already assigned); ethnonym-clan-adjective.
Longing/lacking; from √avah (to long for); social underclass alongside ani and dal; the hyphenated English captures lack-plus-longing.
Hapax Eccl 12:5 caper-berry-fails-stimulus; plant-identity uncertain but capparis-tradition.
Proper noun, Benjamin-son of Shaharaim; 1Chr 8:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abitub.

2S-the-fifth-Shephatiah-the-son-of-Abital and 1Chr-the-fifth-Shephatiah-of-Abital (2S 3:4; 1Chr 3:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abital-wife-David-mother-Shephatiah-aspect from other Abi-names; family with H1 av 'father' (already assigned) - 'my-father-is-dew'-theophoric-David's-fifth-wife-Hebron.
King of Judah, son of Rehoboam (1Kgs 14:31; 15:1,7,8; 2Chr 11:20,22; 12:16). English convention: Abijam. 'Father-of-sea'. Distinguished from H29 Abijah (same person, different name-form).

Gen-Joktan-begat-Obal-Abimael-Sheba and 1Chr-Abimael (Gen 10:28; 1Chr 1:22). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abimael-son-Joktan-Arabian-tribe-aspect from other theophoric-names; 'my-father-is-God'-patronymic-Joktanite.
Proper noun ('my father is king'); concordantly transliterated; multiple persons in the Tanakh.

Multiple persons: son of Jesse (1Sam 16:8), keeper of the ark (1Sam 7:1), son of Saul (1Sam 31:2), district-officer under Solomon (1Kgs 4:11); concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abinadab.
Father of judge Barak from Kedesh (Judg 4:6,12; 5:1,12). English convention: Abinoam. 'Father-of-pleasantness'; family with H5278 no'am 'pleasantness'.

Ebiasaph-Korahite-Levitical-genealogy and temple-singers-descent (1Chr 6:8,22; 9:19). English convention: Ebiasaph. 'My-father-has-gathered' or 'father-of-gathering' (av-father + asaph-gather already assigned).
Manassite tribe-head and Gideon's family-clan (Josh 17:2; Judg 6:34; 8:2; 2Sam 23:27; 1Chr 7:18; 11:28; 27:12). 'My-father-is-help'. English convention: Abiezer.
Proper noun, one of David's mighty men, an Arbathite; 2Sam 23:31; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abi-albon.

Mighty-bull as title of Jacob's God or as leader-stallion (Gen 49:24; Ps 132:2,5; Isa 1:24; 49:26; 60:16). Hyphenated to distinguish the bull-mighty-divine-title from H47 abbir 'strong-mighty' (the adjective).
Poetic term for bull, warrior, bird-of-prey (strength); the hyphenated English marks intensity. Family with H46 abir 'bull-mighty' (the noun-title).

Son of Eliab, Reubenite who rebelled with Dathan and Korah against Moses (Num 16:1,12,24,25,27, 26:9, Deut 11:6, Ps 106:17 earth swallows up); also firstborn of Hiel at Jericho-rebuilding (1Kgs 16:34); 'my-father-is-exalted'; concordantly transliterated.
Shunammite who warmed David in his old age (1Kgs 1:3,15; 2:17,21,22). English convention: Abishag. 'My-father-is-wanderer'.
Priest-descendant of Phinehas, and Benjamite (1Chr 5:30,31; 6:35; 8:4; Ezra 7:5). English convention: Abishua. 'Father-is-salvation'.

1Chr-and-Shammai-the-brother-of-Jada-Nadab-and-Abishur and 1Chr-and-the-name-of-the-wife-of-Abishur-was-Abihail-and-she-bore-him-Ahban-and-Molid (1Chr 2:28,29). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abishur-son-Shammai-married-Abihail-Ahban-Molid-aspect from other Abi-names; family with H1 av 'father' (already assigned) - 'my-father-is-wall'-pn-Shammai-second-son-wife-Abihail-two-sons-Jerahmeel-side-line-Caleb-brother.
Proper noun ('father-of-gift'); brother of Joab, captain under David; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abishai.
Proper noun. English convention Absalom.
Proper noun ('father-of-abundance'); priest under David; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abiathar.
Hithpael; smoke-up-rises from wicked-people; Isa 9:18.
Qal/Hithpael: give expression to grief over a deceased one or a calamity; concordantly 'mourn'.

Participle of aval 'mourn'. The mourning one as state-designation (Gen 37:35; Isa 57:18; 61:2,3; Lam 1:4; Esth 6:12; Job 29:25; Ps 35:14). Distinguished from H56 aval 'mourn' (verb) and H60 evel 'mourning' (noun).
Northern border-city near Dan and mourning-name (1Sam 6:18; 2Sam 20:14,15,18). English convention: Abel. 'Meadow-pasture-place'. Distinguished from H1893 Hevel-Abel-person (already assigned).
From √aval (to grieve); state of sorrow with outward sign; concordantly 'mourning'.

Affirmative/adversative particle 'truly' or 'however'; confession (Gen 42:21 Joseph's-brothers 'truly we are guilty'), promise-confirmation (Gen 17:19 'verily Sarah shall bear'), court-politics (2Sam 14:5, 1Kgs 1:43), realisation (2Kgs 4:14 Shunammite-childless), prophetic-insight (Dan 10:7,21), administrative (Ezra 10:13, 2Chr 1:4, 19:3, 33:17); concordantly 'verily'. Distinguished from H56 aval 'mourn' (verb-homonym).

1K-and-he-smote-Ijon-and-Dan-and-Abel-Beth-Maacah-and-all-Chinneroth and 2K-he-took-Ijon-and-Abel-Beth-Maacah-and-Janoah (1K 15:20; 2K 15:29). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abel-Beth-Maacah-Naphtali-northern-city-aspect from H1038 Beth-Maacah-alone (already assigned); family with H63 Abel-place and H1004b bayit-house (both already assigned) - 'meadow-house-Maacah'-Dan-Naphtali-Asa-Benhadad-capture-Tiglath-Pileser-exile.
Proper noun ('mourning-acacia-field'), Moab-plain; Num 33:49; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abel-shittim.
Proper noun ('mourning-vineyards'), Jephthah-border; Judg 11:33; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abel-cheramim.

Judg-the-host-fled-as-far-as-Beth-Shittah-toward-Zererah-to-the-border-of-Abel-Meholah and 1K-Elisha-the-son-of-Shaphat-of-Abel-Meholah (Judg 7:22; 1K 19:16). Hyphenated to distinguish the Abel-Meholah-city-Jordan-aspect from other Abel-names; family with H57 avel 'meadow' (already assigned) - 'meadow-of-the-dance'-compound-birthplace-Elisha-Gideon-victory.
Proper noun ('mourning-waters'), variant of Abel-Beth-Maacah; 2Chr 16:4; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abel-maim.
Proper noun ('mourning-of-Egypt'), threshing-floor of Atad; Gen 50:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abel-mizraim.
Unique lexeme. 'Stone' standard.
Aramaic equivalent for building-stone (Ezra 5:8; 6:4; Dan 2:34,35,45; 5:4,23; 6:18). Hyphenated to mark the Aramaic-parallel; family with H68 even 'stone' (Hebrew).

Ex-Pharaoh-to-midwives-when-they-see-on-the-birth-stones and Jer-I-went-down-to-the-house-of-the-potter-he-was-doing-work-on-the-wheels (Ex 1:16; Jer 18:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the birth-stones-potter's-wheel-aspect from H68 even 'stone' (already assigned); dual-form-two-stones-birth-stool-and-potter's-wheel-pair.
River of Damascus 2Kgs 5:12 Naaman-healing-doubt; also Amana-spelling.
Ebenezer-battle-site-and-Samuel-memorial-stone-near-Mizpah (1Sam 4:1; 5:1; 7:12). English convention: Ebenezer. 'Stone-of-help' (even-stone + ezer-help).
Priestly sash/ceremonial girdle (Ex 28:4,39,40; 29:9; 39:29; Lev 8:7,13; 16:4; Isa 22:21). Hyphenated; distinguished from H2290 chagorah 'girdle' (military) and emphasises the band-character.
Proper noun ('father-is-light' or 'my-father-is-ner'); commander of Saul's army; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Abner.

1K-ten-fat-oxen-and-twenty-pasture-oxen-and-a-hundred-sheep and Prov-better-is-a-dish-of-green-herbs-where-love-is-than-a-fatted-ox-and-hatred-with-it (1K 4:23; Prov 15:17). Hyphenated to distinguish the fattened-stall-fed-livestock-fully-fed-aspect from H80 avaq-dust (already assigned) as phonetically-near; Solomon-daily-royal-provision-Proverbs-love-above-luxury-said.

Ex-and-it-shall-become-dust-on-all-the-land-Egypt-and-on-man-and-on-beast-boils-breaking-out-with-blisters and Ex-boils-breaking-out-pustules (Ex 9:9,10). Hyphenated to distinguish the boils-blisters-pustules-aspect from H1158 ba'ah 'boil-up' (possible-root); sixth-plague-skin-disease-specific-term-unique.
Proper noun, Issachar-city; Josh 19:20; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Ebez.

Judg-after-him-Ibzan-judged-Israel-who-was-of-Bethlehem and Judg-he-judged-Israel-seven-years-and-Ibzan-died (Judg 12:8,10). Hyphenated to distinguish the Ibzan-judge-Bethlehem-aspect from other names; minor-judge-between-Jephthah-and-Elon-thirty-sons-thirty-daughters-Bethlehem-Judah.

Gen-a-man-wrestled-with-Jacob-until-the-dawn-rising and Gen-while-he-wrestled-with-him (Gen 32:25,26). Hyphenated to distinguish the wrestle-raise-dust-aspect from H80 avaq 'dust-powder' (already assigned) as same-root-verbal-form; Jacob-Peniel-angel-fight-imagery-dust-whirling.
Finely-pulverised dust of soot or cattle-hoof (Ex 9:9; Deut 28:24; Isa 5:24; 29:5; Eze 26:10; Nah 1:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the fine-grained powder-dust from H6083 afar 'earth-dust' (coarser).
Frankincense-and-myrrh powders bridal-procession; Song 3:6.
Hiphil; hawk-spreads-wings towards south; Job 39:26.

Ps-dove-with-silver-wings-flying and Isa-eagles-wings-strength and Eze-great-eagle-mighty-wings (Ps 55:7; Isa 40:31; Eze 17:3). Hyphenated to distinguish the wing-pinion-flight-feather-wing-stroke-aspect from H3671a kanaf 'wing' (already assigned) and H82 avar-verb 'rise-up-fly' (already assigned); family with H82 avar - poetic-bird-wing-side-form.

Eagle-pinion-image of protection (Deut 32:11; Job 39:13; Ps 68:14; 91:4). Hyphenated to distinguish the pinion-feather-aspect from H5133 notsah 'feathers-plume' and H3671 kanaf 'wing'; family with H83 aver 'great-wing'.
Proper noun; extended form of Avram (H87). English convention Abraham.
Heraldic exclamation for Joseph; Gen 41:43; concordantly transliterated. Etymology uncertain (possibly Egyptian loan); the kneel-down sense is followed by tradition.
Proper noun ('high father'); pre-covenant name; concordantly transliterated (distinguished from Abraham H85).
Stopping-place on the exodus-route eastern-Edom (Num 21:10,11; 33:43,44). English convention: Oboth. 'Water-skins-leather-pouches'.
Proper noun, father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men; 2Sam 23:11; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Agee.
Amalekite king-type (Num 24:7; 1Sam 15:8,9,20,32,33; Esth 3:1,10; 8:3,5; 9:24 Agagite). English convention: Agag.
Descent-designation of Amalek-king Agag (Esth 3:1,10; 8:3,5; 9:24). Gentilic; family with H90 Agag.

Bound-together hyssop-bunch or troops-band (Ex 12:22; 2Sam 2:25; Amos 9:6; Isa 58:6). Hyphenated to distinguish the bundle-binding-aspect from H6014a amar-II 'bind-stack' and H485 allumah 'bound-grain-sheaf' (already assigned); family with H97 agam 'reeds'.
Bridegroom-went-down to nut-garden; Song 6:11.
Proper noun, son-of-Yake-proverb-maker; Prov 30:1; concordantly transliterated. English convention: Agur.
